messages:
incident-bot: Paging @oncall-network and @alex.kim — alert: MarinerLane (private VPC) reporting intermittent 502s on their tenant NLB, spike in outbound errors to vendor endpoints. Impact: degraded inference calls for ~23% of requests.
oncall-network: I’m on it. Can someone confirm if this is just egress or also ingress? any new deployments?
alex.kim: no deploys in the last hour per deploybot. Traffic spike started ~12:04 UTC. Logs show TLS handshake errors to external endpoint api3.external-mlsvc.net and NLB healthy check failures.
samira: adding tenant context: MarinerLane is on a Dedicated pool (dlx-gpu-4) in a private deployment. Egress goes via customer-attached TGW into a small NAT fleet. We’ve had conntrack issues historically on smaller NATs.
platform-eng: I see NLB target group showing a lot of 502 from our NGINX sidecar. Backend instances still report healthy. Possible upstream packet drops / conntrack.
oncall-network: tagging net-eng: @platform-eng any changes to NLB security groups or ALB listener rules? also request the per-tenant egress path flow logs.
platform-eng: no config changes. pulling flow logs, conntrack counters, and nat instance metrics now.
incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0421-7862 | severity: high | assigned: @oncall-network
oncall-network: Handoff to @alex.kim for customer comms. I’ll own network telemetry and routing.
alex.kim: @samira I’ll draft a short status update for MarinerLane. Can you confirm whether KMS/HSM routing or DNS policies were modified? any config drift on the NAT instances?
samira: no KMS changes. DNS policy had an internal resolver tweak yesterday but should not affect egress. NAT instances show increasing conntrack usage.
platform-eng: logs snippet: 
```
[12:03:54] nginx: upstream prematurely closed connection (502) while reading response
[12:04:02] tls_handshake_error: remote error: handshake failure (ALPN mismatch?)
[12:04:18] conntrack: table full, dropping packet from 10.2.5.12:443
```
oncall-network: conntrack entries spiking: 180k -> 671k in ~2 minutes, per-instance conntrack max configured 65536 on some smaller NAT instances. That explains dropped packets and handshake failures.
samira: MarinerLane’s tenant was configured to use smaller NAT capacity to save cost. We have reserved GPU capacity but not oversized egress. Can we reroute their egress to shared-egress-vpc which has larger NATs?
platform-eng: We can change the route table for the tenant subnets to point to shared-egress attachment on the TGW. That will move sessions to the bigger NAT fleet. Need to coordinate NLB healthcheck leniency and warn customer.
oncall-network: Proposed mitigation: 1) failover MarinerLane egress to shared-egress-vpc via route table change (no code deploy) 2) increase NLB healthcheck interval to reduce spurious 502s during switchover 3) monitor and roll back if latency increases >200ms.
alex.kim: Draft customer message: "We’ve detected increased outbound failures impacting your API calls. Our on-call team identified NAT connection saturation for your tenant routes. We will perform a controlled failover of your egress to our shared egress gateway to restore connectivity. Expect a brief window (1-3 minutes) of elevated errors while routes propagate. We will provide updates every 10 minutes"
samira: sending that now to MarinerLane CS rep; they acknowledged and approve failover.
platform-eng: preflight checklist: - confirm no active long-lived stateful sessions that would be disrupted - backup current route table (rtb-ml-0123) - adjust NLB healthcheck to interval 30s, unhealthy threshold 3 - tag maintenance window
oncall-network: enable conntrack logging and increased sampling on NATs to capture post-mortem. escalation policy: ENG-SRE on standby.
incident-bot: escalation: page ENG-SRE for rollback readiness if RTT > 200ms after change
platform-eng: performing route modification: updating rtb-ml-0123 -> target vpc-peering-shared-egress (changing next-hop on TGW attachment).
oncall-network: Route changed. Monitoring metrics now: egress error rate, NAT conntrack, NLB 5xxs, and p95 latency.
platform-eng: within 60s error rate drop: 23% -> 1.8%. Conntrack on new path stable. NLB 502s reduced significantly.
alex.kim: Customer update posted: "Failover completed. We're seeing a significant reduction in outbound errors. Services should recover fully soon. We'll follow up with RCA and next steps." :thumbsup:
samira: creating follow-up ticket to scale MarinerLane NAT capacity and add guardrails to detect conntrack > 75%. Assigning to infra-owner @josh.
platform-eng: RCA data snapshot: 
```
conntrack peak observed: 671k (kernel drop) vs per-instance max 65,536
nat-ml-01 CPU: 92% during peak
route table change: rtb-ml-0123 -> shared-egress-rt
external vendor error rate spiked due to model fallback retries
```
oncall-network: root cause summary: tenant-specific NAT instance pool undersized -> conntrack exhaustion -> packet drops -> NLB upstream 502s. Triggered by sudden outbound fanout to vendor endpoints (fallback behavior).
alex.kim: Post-incident action owners: infra/josh (NAT autoscaling and pool sizing), platform-eng (NLB healthcheck tuning & routing automation), oncall-network (runbook & alert thresholds), customer-success/samira (communications & SLA review).
incident-bot: Status update: Active mitigation completed. Incident moved to monitoring. RCA and action items required.
samira: Customer confirmed recovery and requested timeline for permanent fix and whether credits are applicable. I’ll coordinate with finance.
josh: I'll draft NAT autoscaling plan: increase per-tenant NAT instance type, add ASG with target tracking on conntrack < 60% threshold. ETA: 48 hours to deploy in staging, 72 hours for prod roll-out with testing.
alex.kim: Can we add an automated runbook play: if per-tenant conntrack > 75% then auto-route to shared-egress and notify oncall? That would mitigate manual steps.
oncall-network: Agreed. Filing ticket for runbook automation and adding an alert: conntrack > 75% -> auto-failover policy.
platform-eng: Adding per-tenant conntrack dashboard and an SLO check for outbound success rate.
samira: Closing customer loop: sending post-incident summary and next steps for fix.
incident-bot: Follow-up meeting scheduled: 2026-04-22 15:00 UTC with infra, platform, network, and CS.
summary: Nat saturation caused tenant egress failure leading to 502s on NLB. Mitigated by route failover to shared egress. Actions: NAT autoscaling, runbook automation, dashboards, customer comms.
